crime_highlights: Mr. Harry drove the complainant to a remote area by a lake
He ignored a command to stop and drove his vehicle, with the complainant in the passenger seat, into a tree
He later collided with a second police vehicle and was apprehended
rationale_highlights: The Gladue report thoroughly canvasses the systemic and background factors of Mr. Harry which may bear upon his moral culpability
Tragically, Mr. Harry was born into the cycle of community trauma and intergenerational cultural violence that colonial policies have caused.
Taking into account Mr. Harry's Indigenous heritage and the painful effects of colonialism on his upbringing, particularly his mother's experience
I am prepared to reduce the global sentence to a period of four years in prison to address the reduction in blameworthiness attributable to Mr. Harry's status
note: Crime passage has little victim harm; harm is in para 66, not adjacent.

crime_highlights: On July 3 and 4, 2019, Mr. Handule and Mr. Abdullahi created videos of Mr. Hue.
Though Mr. Hue was aware that the videos were staged, he was fearful about what was going to happen to him.
One video series showed Mr. Hue in his underwear, in the bathtub, with a gun pointed at him.
His feet and hands are bound with purple twine, and a man with a hoodie is standing over him, pointing two guns at his head through a pillow.
Another video showed Mr. Hue crying as he recited a memory about his grandmother.
rationale_highlights: I am satisfied that there is ample evidence before me to support a finding that there is a connection between the systemic racism and discriminatory policies that impact our communities and Mr. Abdullahi's involvement with the criminal justice system.
At a young age, he was exposed to guns, violence and death and was provided little support to manage the trauma he faced.
a CSO in this case would better serve the aims of rehabilitation while also helping to address the societal disadvantages caused to Mr. Abdullahi by systemic racism.
note: Two offenders; rationale is about Abdullahi. Principle on discrimination in paras 236 not included.

crime_highlights: Mr. Wesley lured Mr. Hood to Clearbrook Park in the early morning hours of July 5.
Mr. Wesley approached Mr. Hood from behind and attempted to strangle him with the wire.
Mr. Wesley carried on and stabbed Mr. Hood some 19 times.
Mr. Wesley overpowered him, took the knife, and continued to stab Mr. Hood.
Mr. Wesley remained at the scene and watched Mr. Hood die from his injuries.
rationale_highlights: I am mindful that Mr. Wesley is Indigenous.
It is apparent that Mr. Wesley has had a difficult upbringing.
I am also mindful of the colonial impact that Indigenous people have suffered. I have taken into account all of the Gladue principles and considerations.
Mr. Wesley is still young, he is an Indigenous offender
note: Court only says Gladue considered; never states effect on sentence.
